question: Which Linux companion-app architecture should OpenClaw pursue as the supported path now that Windows Hub is shipped?
rationale: Current main does not implement Linux companion support, and the open candidates differ in language/runtime, dependency graph, gateway contract coverage, proof state, and security review surface.

options.title: Select one Linux native track
options.body: Pick either the C/GTK or Rust/GTK candidate as the canonical Linux app direction, require current-head runtime proof plus security/packaging review, and close or redirect the other track.

options.title: Defer Linux app landing
options.body: Leave the umbrella open but pause large app PRs until maintainers write a thinner architecture brief and acceptance matrix for Linux packaging, auth, node mode, and gateway management.

options.title: Split by platform and capability
options.body: Close the Windows portion as shipped in follow-up triage and create narrower Linux issues for tray, onboarding, gateway management, notifications, and packaging before merging any large app branch.

recommendation.title: Select one Linux native track
recommendation.body: Pick either the C/GTK or Rust/GTK candidate as the canonical Linux app direction, require current-head runtime proof plus security/packaging review, and close or redirect the other track.
